title: Air Inter 148

agencies.name: Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety

summary: Air Inter Flight 148 crashed into Mont Sainte-Odile in the Vosges Mountains while approaching Strasbourg Airport. The pilots set the autopilot to Vertical Speed Mode instead of Flight Path Angle Mode, then entered a descent rate of 3300 feet per minute instead of the intended 3.3 degrees. The ambiguous autopilot display showed only two digits, masking the actual high descent rate. The aircraft lacked a ground proximity warning system that might have alerted the crew.
probable_cause: The crew set the autopilot to the wrong mode and misread the descent setting on an ambiguous display, entering a steep descent of 3300 feet per minute. The absence of a ground proximity warning system deprived the pilots of an alert to the terrain impact.

factors.evidence: the display showing the descent rate in feet only showed the first two digits, so 3,300 feet per minute would be displayed as 33
pilots left the autopilot set in Vertical Speed Mode, which uses feet per minute, instead of Flight Path Angle Mode, which uses the angle
pilots did not monitor as the aircraft entered a high descent rate of 3300 ft per minute
Air Inter had not equipped its aircraft with a ground proximity warning system (GPWS)
Aircraft crashed into the slopes of Mont Sainte-Odile at 2,620 ft

events.text: Flight cleared to descend to 5000 ft and vectored to ANDLO waypoint
Autopilot set to Vertical Speed Mode and descent set, aircraft entered high descent rate
Aircraft entered a high descent rate of 3300 ft per minute without crew detection
Aircraft crashed into the slopes of Mont Sainte-Odile at 2,620 ft, 10.5 nautical miles from the airport

title: Thai Airways International 311
summary: Thai Airways Flight 311 crashed into mountainous terrain north of Kathmandu during approach. After encountering a minor flap malfunction and instrument conditions, the captain became disoriented due to poor visibility, frustration with ATC communication, and a weak first officer, making a 360-degree turn instead of returning to the initial approach fix and flying directly toward the mountains.
probable_cause: Loss of situational awareness by captain and ATC controller; language and technical communication problems causing captain frustration and high workload; first officer's lack of initiative; inadequate training for the complex Kathmandu approach; improper FMS use.

factors.evidence: instrument approach with poor visibility
poor visibility and weather conditions
captain extremely frustrated with ATC and inconclusive answers
first officer's lack of initiative and inconclusive answers
captain forced to resolve complex approach himself
captain unintentionally made nearly 360° turn instead of 180°
aircraft passed over airport northbound and headed toward Himalayas
aircraft crashed into mountain 37 km north of Kathmandu

events.text: Flight 311 departed Bangkok for Kathmandu

Aircraft descended back to 11,500 ft and made nearly 360° turn instead of 180° turn
GPWS activated warning of imminent collision with mountains
Aircraft crashed into mountainside 37 km north of Kathmandu

title: Aeroflot 2808
summary: Aeroflot Flight 2808 crashed into buildings in Lebyazhy Lug village while attempting to land at Ivanovo. The investigation found that the captain continued the approach under unsuitable parameters, the crew failed to follow proper procedures and communicate effectively, and the navigator had not set the correct altimeter pressure. These factors combined with failure to follow descent rate guidelines led to navigation errors and loss of control during the final descent.
probable_cause: The primary cause was the captain's decision to continue the approach under unsuitable parameters. Insufficient crew communication and poor cockpit resource management, combined with failure to follow maximum descent rate guidelines and an altimeter setting error by the navigator, led to loss of control and terrain impact.

factors.evidence: Insufficient crew communication and poor cockpit resource management also led to periodic loss of control

the navigator forgot to set his altimeter to the correct pressure

The air traffic controller at Ivanovo airport acted in violation of aviation guidelines by not notifying the crew about their deviations from the course and glide path

title: PIA 268
summary: PIA Flight 268 descended below cleared altitude during approach and crashed into the 8,250 ft Mahabharat Range mountain at Bhattedanda. The aircraft initiated each descent step too early, descending 1,300 feet below cleared altitude by the Sierra reporting point. Investigators determined pilot error as the primary cause, with contributions from poor visibility, lack of radar surveillance, and unclear approach plates.
probable_cause: Pilot error: the aircraft initiated each step of descent one step too early, approaching the Mahabharat Range at insufficient altitude. The lack of radar prevented controllers from warning of inappropriate altitude.

factors.evidence: The aircraft initiated each step of its descent one step too early.
The aircraft approached the Mahabharat Range at an insufficient altitude and crashed into the south slope.
Visibility was poor due to overcast conditions.
The approach plates for Kathmandu issued to PIA pilots were also determined to be unclear.
The aircraft crashed at approximately 7300 ft into the side of the 8,250 ft mountain at Bhattedanda, disintegrating on impact.

events.text: The aircraft was cleared for an approach from the south called the Sierra approach.
The aircraft was to then descend in seven steps to 5,800 feet.
The aircraft initiated each step of its descent one step too early.
The aircraft crashed at approximately 7300 ft into the side of the 8,250 ft mountain at Bhattedanda.

title: El Al 1862
summary: The Boeing 747-200F cargo aircraft experienced separation of engines 3 and 4 from the right wing shortly after departure from Schiphol. Engine 3 separated and damaged engine 4, ripping out a 10-meter stretch of the wing's leading edge. The aircraft became uncontrollable and crashed into apartment buildings in the Bijlmermeer neighbourhood of Amsterdam, destroying dozens of apartments.
probable_cause: Separation of engine 3 (inboard right) from the aircraft, which subsequently damaged and separated engine 4, causing total loss of control and structural damage to the right wing.

factors.evidence: At 18:27, witnesses heard a sharp bang and saw falling debris; the No.3 (inner right) engine separated from the right wing of the aircraft
The No.3 engine separated from the right wing, shot forward, damaged the wing slats, then fell back and struck the No.4 engine, tearing it from the wing
The separation of engines ripped out a 10 m stretch of the wing's leading edge and caused total loss of wing structural integrity
The aircraft became totally uncontrollable after losing both right-side engines and wing structure
At 18:35:42, the aircraft nose-dived and crashed into two high-rise apartment complexes in Bijlmermeer neighbourhood, exploding in a fireball

title: Libyan Arab Airlines 1103
summary: Flight 1103, a Boeing 727 with 159 people on board, was on approach to Tripoli. At 3161 ft above sea level during approach, the aircraft's tail collided with a Libyan Air Force MiG-23UB right wing and the Boeing disintegrated, killing all 159 passengers and crew. The two MiG-23 crew members ejected and survived. The official investigation concluded the cause was collision with the military aircraft.
probable_cause: Collision with a Libyan Air Force MiG-23 during approach to Tripoli International Airport at 3161 ft altitude.

factors.evidence: the aircraft's tail collided with a Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23's right wing and disintegrated
official explanation and air accident investigation report both blamed a collision with a Libyan Air Force MiG-23
two air traffic controllers on duty that day, including one civilian controller and one military controller
two air traffic controllers on duty, including one civilian controller still undergoing training under supervision of a military controller

events.text: Flight 1103 took off from Benina International Airport near Benghazi on a domestic flight to Tripoli International Airport.
During approach to Tripoli, the aircraft was at an altitude of 3161 ft above sea level.
The aircraft's tail collided with a Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23's right wing and disintegrated.
All 159 passengers and crew were killed while the two MiG-23 crew members ejected and survived.
